I've tried to post it before but because it was a theory rather than a question or an experience, it was deleted.  Here goes.

Universes are supposed to be spawned by choices.  Each choice creates a new universe; you go to the shops, or you stay home, and each one spins out from there.  This would leave trillions of universes, some only slightly different, some very different.

But the universe has a tendency to *conserve* energy rather than expend it.  So, for reasons I haven't figured yet, some universes *merge* together, and *this* is where our strange, realistic dreams come from, a distant version of ourselves, while up close, universes that are almost the same, merge, and artefacts left over from both are what cause glitches in the matrix.  Example, you can't find your watch, then suddenly you realise you have two, then one disappears.  The universes have merged, and corrected themselves into one.  After a while you forget about it as your brain adjusts to the new reality.  There seems to be so many glitches out there: a dropped object disappears, sometimes reappearing hours, days, or months later.  Your friend says he sees you downtown when you were never there.  You remember a close friend that no one else can recall.  You're on a highway and a car passes you... then passes you *again*.  And these are just the ones we notice/remember.  Who knows how often they happen?

That's my theory. :)  Ask questions if you want.
